title: TPM presence and state
whyItMatters: A TPM changes how BitLocker keys are protected and what must be considered before the machine leaves the owner's control.
notes: Read-only CIM query of the two initial-state properties. No TPM method is invoked and no ownership is changed. Absent on machines without a TPM.

cleanup.risk: A TPM is a chip state, not stored personal data, so there is nothing on this PC to delete. Clearing TPM ownership is an administrator decision that a reset of this PC already makes.
cleanup.reason: This is a hardware fact about the machine, not a file or setting that holds personal data, so there is nothing to remove here.
cleanup.source: Microsoft Learn, Trusted Platform Module (TPM) overview: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/security/hardware-security/tpm/trusted-platform-module-overview
